name: Carina Nebula
tagline: The southern sky's great star factory — home to the doomed hypergiant Eta Carinae.
history: The Carina Nebula is one of the galaxy's largest star-forming complexes — a 300-light-year cauldron of gas and dust where some of the heaviest known stars are born and die. Its centerpiece, Eta Carinae, erupted in the 1840s into the second-brightest star in the sky and is now a candidate for the next nearby supernova or even a gamma-ray burst. Hubble's 'Mystic Mountain' pillar image made its newborn-star nurseries iconic.
